title: Auto Loans: days past due, delinquency, cure and charge-off
content:
# Auto Loans: days past due, delinquency, cure and charge-off

This policy of the Auto Loans product category at PCB governs how days past due are counted on an auto loan and how the loan moves between active, delinquent and charged-off status. Each product applies its own delinquency threshold and charge-off threshold, both in days past due.

## Clauses

1. **Days past due** count the calendar days since the earliest unsatisfied installment due date, and return to zero when every past-due installment is satisfied.
2. **Delinquent.** The loan becomes delinquent when its days past due reach the product's delinquency threshold.
3. **Cure.** A delinquent loan returns to active when its days past due return to zero.
4. **Charge-off.** The remaining principal is charged off when the days past due reach the product's charge-off threshold. The charge-off writes off the whole principal balance and the debt passes to recovery; the loan's status becomes charged off.
5. Repossession, settlements, hardship modifications and payment plans for delinquent loans are outside this policy.

Each step is judged from the days past due on PCB's loan record.

## Status ladder

| Days past due on the loan record | Status consequence |
|---|---|
| zero | active (a delinquent loan returns to active) |
| above zero, below the delinquency threshold | an active loan has not yet become delinquent |
| at or above the delinquency threshold, below the charge-off threshold | delinquent |
| at the charge-off threshold | whole principal balance charged off; debt to recovery |

## Counting illustration (hypothetical dates)

The earliest unsatisfied installment was due 2026-04-05. On 2026-05-01 the loan is 26 days past due. If the borrower then satisfies that installment and every later past-due one, the count returns to zero.

## Points of judgement

**Does paying only the most recent missed installment cure a delinquent loan?** No. Days past due return to zero only when every past-due installment is satisfied, and the count runs from the earliest unsatisfied one.

**Is part of the principal kept on the loan after charge-off?** No. The whole principal balance is written off.
